Son of Abraham
suhn uhv AY-bruh-ham
noun
From son + Abraham; a title of natural descent and, more deeply, of the faith that reckons one a true child of the patriarch.

📖 Biblical Definition

A son of Abraham is, in the first sense, a natural descendant of the patriarch through Isaac and Jacob, an Israelite according to the flesh. But Scripture presses the title to a deeper meaning: the true sons of Abraham are not merely those of his blood but those of his faith. They which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham (Gal 3:7); for Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness, and he is the father of all them that believe, whether circumcised or uncircumcised (Rom 4:11). Thus John the Baptist warned the Pharisees not to boast, We have Abraham to our father, for God is able of stones to raise up children unto Abraham; and the Lord told Zacchaeus the publican, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham—reckoning the repentant tax-gatherer a true heir of the promise. To be a son of Abraham in the saving sense is to walk in the steps of that faith which he had, trusting the God who justifies the ungodly. The dictionary honors the title as the charter of the gospel to the nations: that in Abraham’s seed, which is Christ, all the families of the earth are blessed, and every believer made an heir according to the promise.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A descendant of Abraham; more deeply, one who shares his faith. They which are of faith are the children of Abraham, heirs of the promise in Christ.

SON OF ABRAHAM, a descendant of the patriarch; truly, an heir of his faith.

They which are of faith are the children of Abraham (Gal 3:7).

John warned the Pharisees not to boast of Abraham as their father.

Christ named Zacchaeus the publican a son of Abraham by repentance and faith.

In Abraham’s seed, Christ, all families of the earth are blessed.

📖 Key Scripture

Gal 3:7 — "Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham."

Luk 19:9 — "And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham."

Rom 4:11 — "And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:"

Mat 3:9 — "And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sonship to Abraham is claimed by mere descent or by ethnic pride; Scripture reckons the true sons by the faith of Abraham, not the blood alone.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the ancient one the Baptist and the Lord both rebuked: the presumption that natural descent from Abraham secures the promise apart from faith. The Pharisees said, We have Abraham to our father; John answered that God could raise up children to Abraham from stones (Matt 3:9), and the Lord declared that the children of the devil, not of Abraham, are known by their works. Blood without faith does not make a true son.

The principle to recover is that sonship to Abraham is by faith, and so the title is the charter of the gospel to the nations. Abraham was justified by believing God before he was circumcised, that he might be the father of all who believe, Jew and Gentile alike (Rom 4:11). When the Lord called the repentant publican Zacchaeus a son of Abraham (Luke 19:9), He reckoned saving faith, not pedigree, as the mark of the true heir. Every believer in Christ, Abraham’s seed, is thereby a child of the patriarch and an heir according to the promise.
